title: The Rig Veda Whole in Aufrecht's Transliteration (Die Hymnen des Rigveda, second edition, Bonn, 1877)

license.payload: Public domain: the hymns are of the second millennium BCE. Theodor Aufrecht, Die Hymnen des Rigveda, 2nd ed. (Bonn: Marcus, 1877), is public domain. Internet Archive scans of public-domain volumes.

items.work: Theodor Aufrecht, Die Hymnen des Rigveda, 2nd ed., Erster Theil: Maṇḍala I–VI (Bonn: Marcus, 1877); Harvard copy
Theodor Aufrecht, Die Hymnen des Rigveda, 2nd ed., Zweiter Theil: Maṇḍala VII–X (Bonn: Marcus, 1877); University of Michigan copy

scope: All ten maṇḍalas, 1,028 hymns, in the Saṃhitā text in Aufrecht's Latin transliteration, the edition most read in the nineteenth century. Max Müller's Devanāgarī edition with Sāyaṇa's commentary (1849–74) is public domain and not seated in this pass: QUEUED. Digital texts (GRETIL, the Vedaweb corpus) are under their own terms and are not seated.
why_seated: Seated beside the Upanishads already on the shelf: the hymns from which the Vedic tradition the Upanishads close begins, among them the creation hymn (10.129) that asks whether even the one who looks down from the highest heaven knows.
normalization: Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt); the scan under original/<identifier>/ is the witness. Where the text layer is noise over a script (cuneiform, Avestan), the scan is the only reading.
